newsitem.title: USA: Fed's goal is maximum sustainable growth -- Moskow.
newsitem.headline: Fed's goal is maximum sustainable growth -- Moskow.

text.p: The Federal Reserve's monetary policy objective is to help foster maximum sustainable growth, said the president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Michael Moskow.

Moskow, speaking to reporters at the Chicago Fed's Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, was asked about the various theories to explain the current success story of the U.S. economy that combines strong growth, low unemployment and low inflation.

"I don't think we are at a time when we can say the old (supply-and-demand) rules of the economy no longer apply," Moskow said, while acknowledging "we have had seven years of the economy doing very well."

While declining to elaborate on the U.S. monetary policy outlook, Moskow stressed "our objective (at the Fed) is to have maximum sustainable growth on the long-term basis and I emphasize sustainable on a long-term basis."
"The numbers that first came out on the first quarter GDP (Gross Domestic Product) are exactly that. They are one quarter," Moskow pointed out. "The economy was strong, of course."

While noting the economy grew at a rapid pace for two consecutive quarters in October 1996 to March 1997, Moskow cautioned the mild winter weather in some U.S. regions may have contributed to the economic strength.

"Looking forward, I do not expect that level of demand," Moskow said. "As you look forward to the rest of this year, our expectation is that average growth for this year, fourth-quarter over fourth-quarter, will be lower than the rate of growth in the first quarter."
